criteria.semantics: A native <table> whose <caption> names it, its header cells native <th> with scope (col for a header row, row for each row's first cell), its data cells <td>.

keyboard.outcome: Passes it by: it is not a stop in the tab order.
Move to the table, and from cell to cell, each cell read with its headers.

criteria.name: The table's caption.
criteria.role: Table, with its number of rows and columns.
criteria.group: Each data cell's column and row headers, read with it.

setting.statement: WHEN I set my text size to 200% I SEE the cells grow with it, with no loss of information.
WHEN I zoom the page to 400% I SEE the table whole, scrolling inside its own region if it must, with no horizontal scrolling.

check.statement: The face emits a native <table> element.
I SEE a caption that names the table: the table's caption.
The table has header cells, each a <th> with a scope of row or col.
WHEN I reach the table with a desktop screen reader (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) I HEAR its caption and its number of rows and columns.
WHEN I move from cell to cell I HEAR each cell with its column and row headers.
WHEN I swipe through the table with a mobile screen reader (TalkBack, VoiceOver) I HEAR each cell with its headers.

criteria.semantics: The table's caption, then a row of cells per row, header cells in bold, rows separated by a rule. Once GPUI exposes a tree: an AccessKit Table of Rows and Cells, its headers ColumnHeader and RowHeader, named by its caption.

keyboard.outcome: Pass the table by: it is no stop of its own; the controls before and after it are.

criteria.name: The table's caption.
criteria.role: Table, with its rows and columns.

setting.statement: WHEN I set the system text size to 200% (Windows' Accessibility, Text size; GNOME's Large Text or text scaling factor) I SEE the caption and the cells grow with it, with no loss of information.

WHEN I raise the display scale (macOS' Displays, Larger Text; Windows' Scale at 150% or 200%; GNOME's Scale at 200%) I SEE the caption and the cells drawn sharp and larger, whole and without overlapping.

WHEN I turn on the platform's high contrast (macOS' Increase contrast, a Windows contrast theme, the desktop portal's contrast) I SEE the window switch to the high-contrast palette by itself, the caption and the cells at 7:1.
WHEN I choose the high-contrast theme for the window I SEE the caption and the cells drawn in the high-contrast palette, every pair at 7:1.
WHEN I magnify the screen (macOS Zoom, Windows Magnifier, GNOME's Zoom) I SEE the caption and the cells whole and legible in the magnified view.

check.statement: A table adds no stop of its own to the window's tab order.
I SEE the header cells set apart in bold, not only by color.
WHEN I move through the table with VoiceOver (macOS), Narrator (Windows) or Orca (Linux) I HEAR its caption, its size, and each cell with its column and row headers.

announce.api: AXTable of AXRow and AXCell, AXColumnHeaderUIElements and AXRowHeaderUIElements set (AccessKit Role::Table).
announce.says: "Totals, table, 2 rows, 2 columns"; in a cell, "Count, Apples, 3".

announce.api: ControlType Table with the Grid and Table patterns, its cells GridItem and TableItem with their headers.
ATSPI_ROLE_TABLE with the Table interface, its headers ATSPI_ROLE_COLUMN_HEADER and ATSPI_ROLE_ROW_HEADER.

criteria.note: GPUI 0.2.2 exposes no accessibility tree (no AccessKit, NSAccessibility, UI Automation or AT-SPI provider), so every HEAR check is blocked by the toolkit, and so are the system text size and the platform's high contrast, which it does not report. GPUI's main branch has AccessKit (zed-industries/zed#56065), not yet released (gpui/README.md, "Accessibility tree"). Its SEE checks with a probe run on GPUI's test platform (gpui/src/native.rs, every_gpui_see_check_with_a_probe_holds), which no CI job runs yet; the rest are reported as not verified.
